questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

questions.questionText: The government is considering building flood defences along a river. It has calculated the costs and benefits as follows. costs benefits $m $m private 450 260 external 60 190 According to cost-benefit analysis, which decision and reasoning about flood defences is correct? decision reasoning

options.A: build external benefits are greater than external costs
options.B: build social benefits are greater than private benefits
options.C: do not build private costs are greater than the external benefits
options.D: do not build social costs are greater than the social benefits

options.B: an individual firm’s degree of interdependence in the market
options.C: the concentration ratio in the market
options.D: the number of firms in the market

options.D: barriers to entry are high

questions.questionText: The table shows the average incomes of the richest 20% of households and the poorest 20% of households in the UK (2015–2016), and the effects of government taxation and benefits on average income. average income average income (£) of (£) of richest 20% poorest 20% before taxes and benefits 85000 7000 after direct taxes and cash benefits 68000 13000 after all taxes (direct and indirect) and all benefits 63000 17000 What can be concluded from the information in the table?

options.A: The effects of direct taxation have affected the rich less than the poor.
options.B: The government’s policy achieved income equality across households.
options.C: The government redistributed all income taken from the rich to the poor.
options.D: The government’s policy reduced the income inequality between the poor and the rich.

questions.questionText: Assuming there are no externalities, where would a nationalised firm set output to maximise social welfare?

options.A: where average revenue equals average cost
options.B: where average revenue equals marginal cost
options.C: where marginal revenue equals marginal cost
options.D: where marginal revenue is zero

questions.questionText: What is the specific advantage of pollution permits, when compared with an alternative policy of taxes levied on the quantity of pollutants emitted by firms?

options.A: firms have a financial incentive to reduce pollution
options.B: no monitoring of firm’s emissions is required
options.C: pollution levels can be reduced to zero
options.D: the reduction in the level of pollution is more predictable

questions.questionText: Company X reduces its number of workers from 250 to 200 and as a result its output decreases from 5000 to 4800 units per day. Company Y increases its number of workers from 800 to 1000 and as a result its output increases from 2000 to 2200 units per day. What happens to labour productivity of the workers in the two companies? company X company Y

options.A: falls rises
options.B: rises falls
options.C: rises rises
options.D: falls falls
